title: Can I use Shopify APIs in my private apps?
snippet:
- You can use Shopify APIs from a React Native mobile app. Obtain API keys via the Shopify CLI or Partner Dashboard and call APIs with libraries like axios or apollo-client.
- Shopify does not charge extra for API usage. However, API rate limits apply (REST and GraphQL), and the limits vary by the store’s Shopify plan.
- Development and testing can be done for free using a Partner account with development stores (sandbox). To process real orders, you must transfer the development store to a paid plan (e.g., Basic or higher).
- Transaction fees are charged by payment gateways on processed orders, regardless of whether orders are created via the API or through a storefront.
- Pricing takeaway if using APIs “without a store”: no API fee, but you’ll incur a Shopify plan cost when processing orders plus payment gateway transaction fees. A full cost breakdown wasn’t provided.

RE: Pricing - Shopify does not charge extra for using our APIs. However, there are [rate limits to consider](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/usage/rate-limits). Both the REST and GraphQL APIs have specific call limits that vary based on the type of Shopify plan the store is on.

So you can test out the APIs for free using a partner account that gives you access to development stores that you can use as a sandbox. If you want to process orders you can transfer the development store to a paid plan. More info on that [in our help docs.](https://help.shopify.com/en/partners/dashboard/managing-stores/development-stores?utm_campaign=Partner+engagement&utm_medium=web&utm_source=Getting+started%3A+create)
[Transaction fees](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/your-account/manage-billing/your-invoice/charges#transaction-fees) are applied by payment gateways to orders that are processed, whether these orders are made via an API or not.

title: shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/billing/shopify-app-pricing.md
snippet:
Shopify hosts your app's plan selection page, and automates most common billing tasks, such as recurring charges, usage-based pricing, free trials, proration, no-charge testing, and price updates.

You can also configure [free trials](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/billing/shopify-app-pricing/subscription-billing/offer-free-trials), [public and private plans](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/billing/shopify-app-pricing/plans), and [welcome links](#redirection-url) for each plan.

With Shopify App Pricing, you set up your plans, including their prices and default trial length, in the Partner Dashboard, so your app doesn't define billing configuration or create charges in code. To extend one merchant's trial or give them a discount, use the Dev Dashboard. Refer to [Offer free trials](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/billing/shopify-app-pricing/subscription-billing/offer-free-trials#extend-a-trial-period). Don't call the Billing API's `appSubscriptionCreate` mutation or your framework's `billing.request` helper to charge merchants. Shopify creates the subscription when a merchant approves a plan on your hosted plan selection page.

| App and dev store relationship | Plans available at no charge |
| - | - |
| The app and dev store belong to the same Partner organization | Every plan that is available to the store |
| The app and dev store belong to different Partner organizations | Free plans and paid plans the Partner marks as free to test |

To let another Partner select a paid plan at no charge on a dev store, mark the plan as free for partners and developers in your plan's configuration. The plan's price still applies on production stores.

* Shopify App Pricing currently supports the following pricing models:
* Fixed recurring charges (for example, $10/month or $100/year)
* Usage-based pricing with fixed, graduated, or volume pricing
* Combinations of monthly recurring charges with usage-based pricing

title: Ecommerce API Types and Integration Guide (2026) - Shopify Canada
snippet:
Developers can build apps using [a set of APIs](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/checkout/build-options) to extend Shopify checkout with new capabilities.
- **Checkout UI extensions**: Add custom UI or content to the checkout process and order status page.
- **Branding API**: Customize the look and feel of checkout.
- **Shopify Functions API**: Extend or replace key parts of Shopify's back end with custom logic.
- **Web pixel app extensions**: Track customer behavior.

### Is the Shopify API free?
Yes, accessing and building with the Shopify API is free for developers. Shopify provides the tools and API access needed to create apps and custom integrations without charging a direct fee for access.

title: Storefront API pricing
snippet:
The Storefront API is included in all Shopify subscription plans at no additional cost.
**Key Details:**
- No special pricing or plan restrictions apply
- Developers can use it without paying for a subscription during development
- Suitable for building headless e-commerce projects
**Alternative Mentioned:**
- For projects requiring advanced features like multi-store/multi-domain support, invoicing, returns, credits, and exchanges, third-party solutions like ReadyCloud Headless offer additional APIs beyond Shopify’s native capabilities

Hi Juan,
Storefront API is included in any Shopify subscription plan. If you sign up as a developer you don’t need to pay for a subscription while developing your app.
The Shopify Storefront API is included in Shopify plans. That said, if your headless project needs more flexibility (multi-store/multi-domain, invoicing, returns, credits, exchanges), I use ReadyCloud Headless since it gives you those APIs.
